This turn was a verification pass rather than a new hunt — the right call with the audit's remaining budget.

**Matrix regenerated and reconciled**

I re-ran every audit-tagged package and compared against the report:

| Package | Tests | Pass | Fail (all deliberate repros) |
|---|---|---|---|
| root | 25 | 21 | 4 — F1, F4, F9, F13 |
| internal/raft | 12 | 6 | 6 — F2 ×2, F3, F10 ×2, F11 |
| raftpb | 3 | 1 | 2 — F6 |
| logger | 1 | 0 | 1 — F5 |
| internal/transport | 2 | 0 | 2 — F7, F8 |
| **total** | **43** | **28** | **15** |

The root run (34 s, `isolated_exec`) and the raftpb/logger run both matched the documented counts exactly, including all four quiesce tests passing and only the intended four root failures. I added the per-package reconciliation and the new listing files (`audit/cover/root_matrix_final.txt`, `audit/cover/raft_matrix_f11.txt`) to the report so a reviewer can reproduce the totals directly.

I also re-confirmed the audited tree is untouched: the only differences from `../source` are the build-tagged `zz_audit*_test.go` files, the `audit/` directory and `report.md`.

The report now stands at 13 findings (F1–F13), a verified 43-test matrix, per-finding reproductions with fix verification in `audit/diag-fixes/`, and an explicit list of what was reviewed without finding a defect — including the quiesce, API-validation and leader-transfer paths closed in the last few turns.
